title: Traffic Report from Raw Logs
description: Answer three questions about web traffic by combining small text tools into pipelines.
scenario: The monitoring dashboard is down, but the product team needs traffic numbers right now for the staging API. The raw access log is at /var/log/app/access.log. Everything they asked for can be answered by chaining small text tools — the classic Unix way — and writing the answers into a report file.
symptoms: The dashboard is unavailable, so numbers must be pulled from raw logs
/var/log/app/access.log holds one line per HTTP request
The product team wants: total requests, how many were 404s, and the noisiest client IP
The answers must land in /home/intern/report.txt in key=value form
mission: Create /home/intern/report.txt with exactly three lines: total=40, errors_404=14 and top_client=10.0.0.5, computed from the real log with shell pipelines.

hints.title: Count lines
hints.content: `wc -l` counts lines. The report format is total=<number>, e.g. total=42.

hints.title: Filter then count
hints.content: `grep -c ' 404 '` prints only a count of matching lines. The status is surrounded by spaces in the log, which keeps the match exact.

hints.title: Top talker pipeline
hints.content: `awk '{print $1}'` takes the first column (the IP). Piping through `sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -1` yields the most frequent one. Prefix the report line as top_client=<ip>.
